newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan firm to bid for wheat shipment deal.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan firm to bid for wheat shipment deal.

text.p: State-run Pakistan National Shipping Corp (PNSC) will bid for a contract to transport wheat expected to be bought by the Pakistani government soon, a company official said on Wednesday.
"The PNSC will submit the lowest bid, as before, for transportation of wheat to be purchased by Pakistan in the next few days," said the official, who asked not to be identified.
The Food and Agriculture Ministry is due to open bids in Islamabad on Sunday in what is expected to be a keenly contested tender for 312,000 tonnes of U.S. or Australian white wheat.

The PNSC official said the corporation had played an important role in stabilising freight rates in the past by bidding at $32 per tonne to transport U.S. wheat, compared to bids of up to $50 per tonne from its competitors.
The PNSC has preferential bidding rights known as first right of refusal in the award of freight contracts -- a system some U.S. officials say deters competitive bidding.
The official said the PNSC was likely to hire or charter bulk carriers to transport wheat on a voyage basis as some of its ships were already on charter abroad.
